data.claim: Optional event fields fold to defaults; new kind is reported by skipped-kinds
data.falsifier: an old event fails to fold or sets a non-empty new field
data.question: Do old events and an old ddflow survive new optional bug fields and a new event kind?

chunk_findings.detail: The handler fabricates a send timestamp for reports that were never sent. Every other field merge (`upstream_url`, `upstream_number`, `upstream_delivery`, `upstream_digest`) leaves the field empty when the event carries nothing, but `upstream_sent_at` falls back to `ev.ts`. The docstring itself calls out the "prepared report with no url yet" case, i.e. an event that records a *proposal*, not a delivery: folding `bug.reported_upstream {delivery: "proposed", digest: "..."}` at t1 sets `bug.upstream_sent_at = t1`, so a report that was only prepared is recorded as sent. Worse, because the merge never replaces, a later real report event `{url: "https://…", delivery: "sent"}` that omits `sent_at` (the schema marks `sent_at` optional) cannot correct it — `str(d.get("sent_at","") or "")` is `""`, then `or bug.upstream_sent_at` keeps t1, so the bug ends up claiming it was sent at the proposal time t1 rather than when it actually went out. Any status/readout keyed on `upstream_sent_at` (the field name promises "sent", and the intent distinguishes "mode propose" from an actual report) will report a proposed report as already delivered.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/core/model.py:_h_bug_reported_upstream (`bug.upstream_sent_at = ... or ev.ts`)

chunk_findings.detail: The MCP `bug_found` tool's declared payload was widened from `("id",)` to `("id", "offer")`, but the upstream offer is, by the stated design, produced only when the call's scope is `ddflow` ("When scope is ddflow the result ends with a one-line offer"). Scope defaults to `project` in this very hunk — `scope=a.get("scope", "") or "project"` — so the common case is a call with no scope argument. Given input `ddflow_bug_found(summary="x")` (no `scope`), the underlying `bug_found` result has no offer, yet the payload spec unconditionally advertises `"offer"` as a returned key. If the payload extractor indexes the listed keys directly (the contract a fixed payload tuple normally encodes), the default project-scope path raises `KeyError`, i.e. the tool fails for every existing caller that never passed a scope; if it uses `.get`, the response shape for all pre-existing project-scope clients changes to include a spurious/`None` `offer` field, which contradicts "the result ends with a one-line offer" only for ddflow. Either way the payload should be conditional on scope, or the api must be guaranteed to always emit an `offer` key (empty for project); as written the unconditional `"offer"` in the tuple is inconsistent with the conditional production of the offer.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/mcp.py (bug_found `"payload": ("id", "offer")`)

chunk_findings.detail: `upstream_offer(scope, bid)` is called with the *requested* `scope`, never with the scope stored on the bug, and `bid = id or auto_id("B", summary, item)` does not encode `scope`. Concretely: file `bug_found(repo, summary="crash on load", item="T1", scope="ddflow")` and then call `bug_found(repo, summary="crash on load", item="T1")` (the CLI/MCP call for a plain re-report, where `scope` defaults to `"project"`). The second call reuses the same `bid`, and because the append always emits `"scope": scope` (unlike `title`/`severity`, which are dropped when empty via `extra`), it writes a `bug.found` event carrying `scope="project"` for a bug that was filed as ddflow, and `upstream_offer("project", bid)` returns `""`, so the result that should end with the upstream-report offer for that ddflow bug has no `offer` at all. The symmetric case is equally wrong: an existing `scope="project"` bug re-filed with `scope="ddflow"` (same summary+item → same id) returns `offer="This bug is in ddflow itself: …"` even though the record is the project's own bug. The function names the bug's scope in its docstring but has no access to the record's scope, so any call whose requested scope differs from the stored scope produces an offer that is either missing or false.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/knowledge.py:upstream_offer / bug_found

chunk_findings.detail: The handler unconditionally stamps a delivery timestamp on reports that were never delivered. The event shape is `{url, number, delivery, sent_at, digest}`, and a *real* delivery always carries `sent_at`; consequently the fallback `or ev.ts` can only ever fire for events that omit it — i.e. the "prepared" / `mode propose` reports the intent describes (offer to prepare a report, `delivery="propose"`, no url yet). For such an input `{"delivery": "propose"}` (no `sent_at`), the line evaluates to `"" or bug.upstream_sent_at or ev.ts` and stores `upstream_sent_at = ev.ts`, so a merely-proposed report is recorded as if it had been sent. Any consumer that treats a non-empty `upstream_sent_at` as proof of delivery (and the field exists precisely to distinguish "prepared" from "went upstream") will mis-report a proposal as delivered, and if the report is never actually filed the bogus timestamp is never corrected. The safe behaviour is to leave `upstream_sent_at` empty for a `delivery`/`sent_at`-less event, since the merge already preserves an earlier real value.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/core/model.py `_h_bug_reported_upstream` (the `upstream_sent_at` assignment)

chunk_findings.detail: The upstream offer is computed only after the extension branch returns, so a ddflow-scoped report that merges into an existing open bug never gets it. Input: an open bug whose auto id matches (`auto_id("B", summary, item)` is unchanged), plus an `answer` that makes `DD.check_add` return `chk.extension` truthy, with `scope="ddflow"`. The function takes `if chk.extension: return DD.extend(log, cfg, chk, "bug.found")` (added above the `offer = upstream_offer(scope, bid)` line), so the returned outcome has no `offer` field, contradicting the stated behavior that "when scope is ddflow the result ends with a one-line offer". The same path also loses the new scope/severity data: only `title` was added to the `DD.Record` passed to `check_add` (`DD.Record(..., title=title, body=summary, item=item)`), while `scope`/`severity` exist only in the literal dict appended inside the later `with log.transaction():` block. `DD.extend` therefore records the title from the record but silently drops the `scope`/`severity`, so a bug the user explicitly scoped to `ddflow` is folded in as an ordinary project bug with no offer to prepare an upstream report.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/knowledge.py `bug_found` — `if chk.extension: return DD.extend(...)`

chunk_findings.detail:
The handler merges every other field with the "empty never blanks a set value" rule, but for `upstream_sent_at` it adds an unconditional fallback to the event timestamp:

```python
bug.upstream_sent_at = str(d.get("sent_at", "") or "") or bug.upstream_sent_at or ev.ts
```

The handler's own docstring says this event also records a report that "was prepared" (not sent) upstream, and `sent_at` is listed as an *optional* event field. So a prepared-only report is recorded as if it had been sent. Concrete input: append `{"kind": "bug.reported_upstream", "subject": "bug-1", "ts": "2025-01-02T03:04:05Z", "data": {"delivery": "proposed", "digest": "..."}}` (no `sent_at`); the resulting `Bug.upstream_sent_at` is `"2025-01-02T03:04:05Z"` even though nothing was sent at that time. Any consumer that treats a non-empty `upstream_sent_at` as "this bug has already been reported/sent upstream" (e.g. to suppress the one-line `offer` on a later `bug found --scope ddflow`, or to render the report as delivered) is then wrong. Because the merge keeps the value once written, a subsequent prepare/propose event cannot clear it either, so the bogus send time is sticky. Setting `upstream_sent_at` only from an explicit `sent_at` (or only when `delivery` indicates an actual send) would avoid marking a merely prepared report as sent.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/core/model.py:1537 (`_h_bug_reported_upstream`)

chunk_findings.detail: This test folds two `bug.reported_upstream` events for subject `B1` without first emitting a `bug.found` event, then asserts that `fold([prepared, sent]).bugs["B1"]` exists and contains the merged upstream fields. A `bug.reported_upstream` event is supposed to annotate an already-existing bug, as the immediately preceding test demonstrates by supplying `bug.found` first. If the handler is update-only (and `fold` is strict), the lookup raises `KeyError` and the test fails. If the handler auto-creates a bug, the test enshrines a phantom bug produced by a stray upstream event (e.g. a malformed log containing only `bug.reported_upstream` for `B1` would materialize a `B1` bug with no summary). Either way the test does not exercise the intended “prepared then sent” sequence on a real bug; it needs a `bug.found` event before the two upstream events.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_bug_scope.py:test_a_later_upstream_event_fills_what_a_prepared_one_left_empty

chunk_findings.detail:
The change drops the `v != "project"` guard so that any truthy `bg.scope` is now copied into the dedupe row. That guard was not dead code: the *old* write path in `api/knowledge.py` emitted `"scope": scope` unconditionally, and the scope parameter defaults to `"project"` (that is exactly why the new code filters `project` out of `extra`). So every bug record created by the previous version has `bug.found` data with `scope == "project"`, and `_h_bug_found` folds it to `bug.scope == "project"`.

Concretely: for an existing store, `st.bugs[c.id].scope == "project"`, so the new comprehension on line 213 produces `{"severity": ..., "scope": "project", ...}` instead of the previous `{"severity": ...}`. A bug created by the new code (scope suppressed at write time, so `bug.scope == ""`) produces a row with no `scope` key at all. Two records that mean the same thing ("project-scoped bug") now yield two different row shapes, and any consumer that inferred "ddflow-scoped bug" from the mere presence of the `scope` key — the invariant the deleted comment spelled out ("`scope` only when it is the unusual one") — will misclassify every legacy project bug, e.g. emitting an upstream-report offer/note for a bug that lives in the project. This is inconsistent with the same change set, which deliberately stops writing `scope` for `project` on the write path.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/_dedupe.py:213 (`_dedupe.py` row.update block)

chunk_findings.detail: The change rewrites the default-scope assertion from `("", "", "project")` to `("", "", "")`, so a call such as `ddflow bug found --summary "plain one"` now persists `bug.scope == ""`. The change notes say the accepted domain is `project|ddflow` and that the default is `project`, so `""` is not one of the accepted scope values; the file's own comment (`# an unrecorded scope is project`) is a rationalization that paper-overs the discrepancy rather than fixing it. This matters because the canonical scope string used throughout the feature is `"project"` — the sibling test asserts `K.upstream_offer("project", "B1") == ""`, and the event fixtures use `subject="B1"` with project semantics — so any consumer that branches on `bug.scope == "project"` (or that validates `scope in {"project","ddflow"}`) will no longer classify a normally-reported bug as project. The test change therefore locks in a regression in the persisted scope value instead of catching it: the previous assertion was the only place verifying the stored default, and it now blesses an out-of-domain value.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_bug_scope.py:43

chunk_findings.detail: `bug_found`'s MCP payload now declares `offer` unconditionally, but the intent states the offer is produced only when `scope=ddflow`; with the default `scope=project` (`scope=a.get("scope", "") or "project"`), the offer is absent, so a payload builder that indexes declared keys will fail or expose an undefined field for the default call, and the CLI/MCP parity claimed by the change does not hold.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/mcp.py bug_found payload `("id", "offer")`

chunk_findings.detail: The test claims to verify that re-reporting a ddflow-scoped bug without `--scope` does not downgrade it to `project`, but it only inspects `next(iter(_bugs(repo).values()))`. Because `fold` preserves insertion order, that is always the bug created by the first `bug found` call, so the assertion passes whenever that first bug retains `ddflow` — even if the second call never merged into it. Concretely, if dedupe/matching regresses so the second `bug found` creates a *new* bug (e.g. `B-2` with scope `project`), `_bugs(repo)` is `{"B-1": <ddflow>, "B-2": <project>}`, `next(iter(...))` returns `B-1`, and the test is green. It never asserts `len(_bugs(repo)) == 1` or that the returned id is the same bug, so this test cannot distinguish "re-report merged and kept scope" from "re-report spawned a duplicate" — which is exactly the regression it exists to guard against (compare `test_extending_an_open_bug_carries_severity_and_scope_onto_it`, which does assert `len == 1`). On a correct implementation where the event writes `scope="project"` by default, the test would also fail for a reason that has nothing to do with dedupe.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_bug_scope.py:153 (test_a_plain_re_report_keeps_a_ddflow_scoped_bug_ddflow_scoped)

chunk_findings.detail: `BUG_REPORT_COMMAND` is introduced as `""`, and `upstream_offer` short-circuits on `not BUG_REPORT_COMMAND`, so no input in this change can ever produce the offer the intent promises ("When scope is ddflow the result ends with a one-line offer to prepare an upstream report"). Concretely, `bug_found(repo, summary="x", scope="ddflow")` normalises scope to `"ddflow"`, writes `extra = {"scope": "ddflow"}` into the log, then computes `offer = upstream_offer("ddflow", bid)` → `""`, `more = {}`, and returns `O.ok("bug.found", id=bid, **chk.data())` — the returned data has no `offer` key and `upstream_offer` is never reached past its guard. The same is true of the extension branch (`O.ok("bug.found", **out.data)`). Consequently both new ddflow-detection paths (`scope == "ddflow"`, `held.scope == "ddflow"` on line ~520, and `"ddflow" in (scope, stored)` on line ~530) are dead code: a ddflow-scoped bug and a project-scoped bug produce byte-identical results. The module-global is only ever mutated outside this file (the comment's claim that `tests/test_bug_scope.py` pins it to the parser is a test-time seam, not production wiring), so unless some other part of the change assigns it at import/startup, the offer is unreachable for every CLI/MCP caller.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/knowledge.py:upstream_offer (BUG_REPORT_COMMAND)

chunk_findings.detail: The change advertises `offer` as part of the `bug_found` payload for every invocation, but the offer is only produced when `scope == "ddflow"` (the change's own intent: "When scope is ddflow the result ends with a one-line offer…"). `scope` defaults to `project` (`scope=a.get("scope", "") or "project"`), and for project-scope bugs no offer is generated, so `bug_found` called with `summary` alone (the documented default path) now requests a payload key that the result does not contain — the payload extraction for `"offer"` either raises a missing-key error or emits an empty/garbage field for the most common call. The unconditional `("id", "offer")` tuple must not require a field that is only conditionally populated; concrete input: `ddflow_bug_found(summary="x")` (no `scope`), which previously returned `{"id": ...}` and now also demands `offer`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/mcp.py (bug_found tool definition, `"payload": ("id", "offer")`)

chunk_findings.detail: `BUG_REPORT_COMMAND` is defined as `""` in the code under review, and nothing in the change assigns it a value. `upstream_offer()` short-circuits on `not BUG_REPORT_COMMAND` and therefore always returns `""`. Consequently the two call sites (`upstream_offer(...)` in the extension branch and in the non-extension branch) can never produce an offer: `bug_found(repo, summary="x", scope="ddflow")` returns an outcome with no `offer` key, the CLI/MCP render nothing, and the stated requirement "When scope is ddflow the result ends with a one-line offer to prepare an upstream report" is never met. The comment ("the command that prepares the report is not there yet") does not populate the constant at runtime, so any caller that passes the new `scope="ddflow"` field gets a ddflow-scoped bug silently recorded with no offer.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/knowledge.py: BUG_REPORT_COMMAND / upstream_offer

chunk_findings.detail:
The new `--scope` option defaults to the non-empty string `"project"` and `knowledge.py` forwards it unconditionally (`scope=a.scope`), so every `bug found` event now carries `data["scope"] == "project"` even when the user never passed `--scope`. That defeats the preservation logic the model comment relies on: `_h_bug_found` merges with `bug.scope = ev.data.get("scope", "") or bug.scope`, which only keeps the previous value when the incoming value is *empty* — `"project"` is truthy, so it always overwrites. The model comment states the invariant "only `ddflow` is ever written", which the CLI default violates.

Concrete failure: `ddflow bug found --id BUG-1 --scope ddflow --summary a` folds BUG-1 to `scope="ddflow"`. Then a later `ddflow bug found --id BUG-1 --summary b` (no `--scope`, argparse default `"project"`) appends an event with `scope="project"`, and the fold silently rewrites `bug.scope` to `"project"`. The bug is demoted, its ddflow-scoped offer/upstream eligibility is lost, and the previously recorded `bug.reported_upstream` data no longer belongs to a ddflow-scoped bug. Fixing this requires either defaulting `--scope` to `""` (letting `Bug.scope`'s `"project"` default apply on absence) or having the writer omit the default value rather than passing `"project"` into the event.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/commands/knowledge.py:308 (with ddflow/surfaces/cli.py `--scope` and ddflow/core/model.py `_h_bug_found`)

chunk_findings.detail: The test helper `_parser_has_bug_report` introspects the CLI parser via `cli.build_parser()._subparsers._group_actions[0].choices["bug"]`. However, `_subparsers` is an `argparse._SubParsersAction` instance, which does not have a `_group_actions` attribute. Calling this helper therefore raises `AttributeError: '_SubParsersAction' object has no attribute '_group_actions'`. This happens unconditionally when `test_the_upstream_offer_is_made_only_while_the_command_exists` invokes the helper on its first line, causing the test to fail even when the feature is correctly implemented. The bug subparser can be obtained directly as `cli.build_parser()._subparsers.choices["bug"]`.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_bug_scope.py: _parser_has_bug_report

chunk_findings.detail: `BUG_REPORT_COMMAND` is initialized to the empty string and no other assignment to it exists in this change. `upstream_offer` short-circuits on `not BUG_REPORT_COMMAND`, so it returns `""` for every input: for `bug_found(repo, summary="crash", scope="ddflow")` (new record), for a re-report of a `ddflow` bug, and for an extension, `offer` is `""`, `more`/the conditional dict stays empty, and the returned `O.ok("bug.found", ...)` carries no `offer` key. The stated behavior — "When scope is ddflow the result ends with a one-line offer to prepare an upstream report" — therefore never happens; the `scope == "ddflow"` branch of both `return O.ok(...)` sites is dead code as written. The surrounding comment ("tests/test_bug_scope.py pins it to the parser") states the constant is supposed to hold the real command (with `{id}`), which is exactly what a test cannot pin when the value is `""`, so the empty value is the defect, not an intentional gate: `upstream_offer` should be reachable for `scope="ddflow"`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/knowledge.py:460 (`BUG_REPORT_COMMAND` / `upstream_offer`)

chunk_findings.detail: The stated contract is that the one-line upstream-report offer is emitted **only when scope is ddflow** ("When scope is ddflow the result ends with a one-line offer to prepare an upstream report"), i.e. the api result carries an `offer` key conditionally. But the MCP tool now declares `"payload": ("id", "offer")`, which lists `offer` as an unconditional returned field. Concrete failure: an agent calls `ddflow_bug_found` the normal way with no `scope` argument (documented default `project`), the api's `bug_found` yields a result without `offer`, and the payload resolution for the new key has nothing to bind to. Under a strict payload mapping this raises `KeyError: 'offer'` on the primary, default-scope call path (every ordinary `bug found` via MCP); under a lenient mapping it instead emits a spurious/`None` `offer` field for project-scoped bugs, contradicting the "only for ddflow" rule. Either way the declared payload and the conditional-offer behavior disagree; the payload entry should be optional or the api must always return an `offer` value (empty when scope is not ddflow) so the two agree. Note the api lambda in this same hunk forwards `title`/`severity`/`scope` but never anything named `offer`, so nothing in this change guarantees the key the payload now requires.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/mcp.py (bug_found `"payload": ("id", "offer")`)

chunk_findings.detail:
The suite asserts two different wire shapes for the *same* operation, `bug.found` on the default `project` scope, which directly contradicts the change's stated "Parity across CLI and MCP". `test_the_offer_is_produced_once_the_command_is_set` requires the api result to *omit* the key (`assert "offer" not in K.bug_found(repo, summary="y", id="B-p", agent="a").data`), whereas `test_the_default_project_call_carries_a_null_offer` requires the MCP tool result to *contain* it with a null value (`assert not result.get("isError") and body["offer"] is None`). At most one of these can hold for any single implementation:

- If the MCP tool returns the api's `Result.data` verbatim (the natural reading of "parity"), `body` has no `"offer"` key and `body["offer"]` raises `KeyError`, so the MCP test errors.
- If instead the api always emits `offer: None` so the MCP body has the key, the api assertion `"offer" not in ...data` fails.

So the change ships a guaranteed test failure (or, if MCP post-processes by adding `offer: None`, then the CLI `--json` output and the MCP output have different shapes for identical input, which is exactly the CLI/MCP divergence the change claims to eliminate). The demonstrating input is the project-scope call used by both tests (`bug found --summary plain` / `ddflow_bug_found(summary="plain")`): one test says the resulting payload has no `offer` member, the other says it has `offer == null`.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_bug_scope.py:test_the_default_project_call_carries_a_null_offer (and tests/test_bug_scope.py:test_the_offer_is_produced_once_the_command_is_set)

chunk_findings.detail: The extension branch guards the merge with the author's own premise that the target may be a record of another kind (`held = st.bugs.get(target)  # the target may be another kind of record`), but then uses that record inconsistently. Concretely, `answer` can extend a duplicate that resolves to a non-bug record: if `st.bugs.get(target)` returns such a record (the case the comment anticipates), `upstream_offer(scope or (held.scope if held else "project"), target)` evaluates `held.scope` on a record for which the new `scope` field need not exist, raising `AttributeError` instead of returning an outcome. If instead such a target is not tracked in `st.bugs` and `held is None`, the requested `title`/`severity`/`scope` are silently discarded by `if extra and held is not None: log.append(...)`, yet the very next line still derives `offer` from the requested `scope` (`scope or ...`), so `bug_found(..., scope="ddflow", answer=...)` returns an outcome advertising the upstream offer while nothing ddflow-scoped was ever persisted — the offer then disappears on the next report of the same bug (where `held`/`prior` are consulted). Either way the non-`None` vs `None` handling of `held` is not consistent with the comment's stated possibility.
chunk_findings.location: ddflow/api/knowledge.py:520 (`held.scope` / `if extra and held is not None` in the `chk.extension` branch)
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/knowledge.py:520 (`held.scope` / `if extra and held is not None` in the `chk.extension` branch)

chunk_findings.detail: The result of `bug_found` only carries the upstream-report offer when `scope == "ddflow"`; the intent states the one-line offer is appended "when scope is ddflow". For a default call (`scope` omitted, i.e. `"project"`) — the common case — the returned result has no `offer` entry, yet the tool's `payload` spec was changed from `("id",)` to `("id", "offer")`. Any client/response builder that projects the result through this key list will therefore fail (or surface a null field) for every ordinary bug-found call, i.e. the default invocation `bug_found(summary="...")` no longer returns the same shape as before. Either the offer must be unconditionally present in the result (e.g. always set, empty for project scope) or the payload must not require a key that only exists in the ddflow branch. Because the intent explicitly conditions the offer on `scope == "ddflow"`, the unconditional `"offer"` in the payload is inconsistent.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/mcp.py (bug_found tool, `"payload": ("id", "offer")`)
